title: Best Travel Cots UK
short: Ten travel cots tested by parents with real babies and toddlers, compared on safety, set-up, comfort and portability.
intro: A travel cot needs to be quick to put up, sturdy once it's up and comfortable enough for a good night's sleep away from home. This guide is based on Mumsnet's tested roundup (updated June 2026), where vetted parent-testers used each cot with their own babies and toddlers over a number of months, judging safety, ease of putting up, efficiency, comfort and portability. Mumsnet also drew on forum recommendations and advice from baby sleep expert Mandy Gurney. Prices are those quoted at time of writing and change often, so check before buying.

products.name: Travel Cot Light
products.best_for: Parents who want the most comfortable, durable travel cot and will use it often
products.key_spec: Birth to three years, 6kg including carry bag, removable machine-washable mattress and fabric, mesh sides
products.summary: Mumsnet's Best Buy and the one that comes up time and again on their forums. The reviewer found it sturdy, simple to set up and easy to transport, with one of the thickest, comfiest mattresses her toddler has slept on and airy mesh sides. Her two-year-old, who often struggles with new sleep environments, slept soundly with every use. It's one of the more expensive travel cots, and the mattress sits fairly close to the floor, though one side unzips for access.
pros: Durable construction
Very comfy mattress
Mattress and fabric removable and machine-washable
cons: Mattress is fairly close to the floor, though one side unzips
One of the more expensive cots around

products.name: CoZee Go Travel Cot
products.best_for: Families with floor space who want maximum airflow, with a newborn bassinet included
products.key_spec: Birth to three years, four mesh side walls, zip-off bassinet (up to 6 months or 9kg), 6.5kg, travel bag included
products.summary: Mumsnet found a breathable, stylish 3-in-1 with four mesh walls, so you can see your baby from any angle and airflow is maximised for warm weather. The parent-tester scored it very highly over a two-month test, praising its sturdiness and spaciousness, and said it gave her baby the same amount of sleeping space as his usual bed. It takes up a lot of floor space and can be awkward to manoeuvre when assembled.
pros: Mesh sides make it a super-breathable choice for summer
Zip-off bassinet for newborns
Washable fabric lining and travel bag included
cons: Takes up a large amount of floor space
Can be a bit awkward to manoeuvre when assembled

products.name: Stardust Travel Cot
products.best_for: Parents who want to use a travel cot often, including from birth
products.key_spec: Birth to two years, unfolds in one second and folds in three, folds with the mattress in, carrycot insert, 6.7kg, 4-year warranty
products.summary: Mumsnet's tester found it incredibly easy to use, with aerospace-style folding that lets the cot fold flat with the mattress attached, which sets it apart from other travel cots she's tested. It's light to carry, the mattress is comfortable and multi-layered, and mesh panels help air circulate. The carrycot insert lets it act as a bedside crib for co-sleeping away from home. It's expensive and only suitable up to two years.
pros: Great quality mattress
Takes one second to unfold and three to fold
Can be folded with the mattress left in
Carrycot insert for newborns
cons: On the expensive side
Only suitable up to 2 years

products.name: Sleeptight Travel Cot
products.best_for: Occasional trips and grandparents' houses on a tight budget
products.key_spec: Birth to three years, mesh on four sides, carry bag, 8.5kg, assembled 76 x 103 x 73cm
products.summary: Mumsnet's editor has owned hers for over 10 years and used it for around seven as a travel bed and playpen for three children, so she can vouch for its durability. It's robust and simple, with padding over the poles and edges, easy to clean and quick to assemble. The mattress is thin, so she bought a separate one, and covers aren't machine-washable and there are no wheels.
pros: Lightweight and folds compactly into a travel bag
Quick to assemble and fold away
Easy to clean, with mesh sides so you can see baby
cons: Mattress is thinner than some others on the market
Doesn't have wheels

products.name: Slumber Travel Cot
products.best_for: Families who want a travel cot that doubles as a playpen from birth to three
products.key_spec: Birth to three years, 3-in-1 (co-sleeper, playpen, travel cot), sloped sides, zip-up door, 6.25kg
products.summary: Mumsnet found a sleek, simple 3-in-1 whose sloped sides make it harder for toddlers to climb out while leaving plenty of play space, plus a little zip-up door that makes it feel less like a 'baby cage'. The tester found it slightly tricky to assemble the first time but expects so much use that it will become second nature, and called it very good value for a quality product.
pros: 3-in-1 design works as co-sleeper, playpen and travel cot
Sloped sides make it harder for toddlers to climb out
Zip-up door
cons: Can be tricky to put up for the first time
Sloped legs take some getting used to and can be tripped over

products.name: Swift 3-in-1 Travel Cot Playpen
products.best_for: Parents who want a bassinet, travel cot and playpen in one
products.key_spec: Birth to 15kg, one-second fold, two-stage mattress, 7kg, folds to L83 x W25 x H25cm
products.summary: Mumsnet's tester found it sturdy and well made, quick to assemble thanks to the one-second fold, with a thick, spongy, supportive two-stage mattress, and it works very well as a safe playpen. Leaning over to place the baby in was 'a bit back-breaking', which she noted is common to travel cots, and a side zip panel would help. She felt it represents good value for money despite the price.
pros: Easy to fold
Lightweight for its size
Two-stage mattress
cons: Pricey
Leaning over to place the baby in is back-breaking, with no side access

products.name: Sena Aire Travel Cot
products.best_for: Frequent travellers with toddlers who want a roomy, airy premium cot
products.key_spec: Birth to 15kg, breathable mesh sides and ventilated mesh mattress, 12kg, assembled L103 x W76 x H73cm
products.summary: Mumsnet's 4'11" tester found it much easier to set up than previous cots and was impressed by its sturdiness when put through its paces by her toddler, with plenty of space and comfort. Breathable mesh sides and a ventilated mesh mattress help in hot climates. It's premium priced and Mumsnet notes nothing particularly remarkable sets it apart from cheaper peers if you'll only use it once or twice a year.
pros: Easy to assemble
Plenty of space for toddlers inside
Comfortable and designed for maximum airflow
cons: Pricey
Not a lot of outstanding features
Heavy at 12kg

products.name: FoldLite LX Travel Cot
products.best_for: Frequent use and limited storage space
products.key_spec: Birth to three years, two fold modes (Home Fold just 26cm wide), removable infant bassinet, two wheels, 6.78kg
products.summary: Mumsnet's tester found it incredibly easy to put up (it just pops up and clicks in, no instructions needed) with a sturdy structure and a removable bassinet that even fit her pram bassinet. There's a quick fold for speed and an ultra-thin Home Fold for storage, and the base is one of the lowest on their list, good for playpen use. The mattress could be thicker.
pros: Lightweight and easy to fold up and down
Collapses to just 26cm wide
Comes with a removable infant bassinet
Two wheels for easy manoeuvring
cons: The mattress could be thicker

products.name: Kubbie Sleep Travel Cot
products.best_for: New parents who want a co-sleeper they can also travel with
products.key_spec: Birth to three years (15kg), removable bassinet, lift-and-lower side panel, mesh on all sides, 8.79kg
products.summary: Mumsnet called it a real steal for new parents who want their newborn close: compact and versatile, with a removable bassinet that's quick to attach and detach. Their tester Ruth particularly liked the co-sleeper function, with the cot tucked against the bed and height adjustable for night feeds. It's too small to use as a playpen and the material isn't machine-washable.
pros: Lift and lower side panel for easy pick-up and put-down
Compact frame that packs into a travel bag
Mesh panels on all four sides and a padded top rail

Material isn't machine-washable

products.name: Arc 2 Travel Cot
products.best_for: Holidays, public transport and camping, especially for toddlers
products.key_spec: Birth to three years (15kg), tent-style, 2.5kg, insect-proof mesh, colour-coded poles, backpack carry bag
products.summary: Mumsnet's tester liked its tent-like design, close to the floor so there's no risk of falling out, plus the mosquito net. At just 2.5kg it folds into a backpack and works as well outdoors as in, though Mumsnet would recommend it for toddlers rather than newborns. The mattress is thin and the sunshade must be bought separately.

Front panel with safety toggle doubles as an outdoor playpen

guide.q: Do I actually need a travel cot?
guide.a: Not necessarily. Mumsnet says it depends on your lifestyle: if you'll only use one for two weeks a year you could probably do without, and a co-sleeper, Moses basket or pram carrycot may work for a smaller baby. If you travel often or your child will stay with grandparents regularly, a travel cot is a good solution.

guide.q: Are travel cots safe for sleeping?
guide.a: Yes if used as intended. Check the cot meets current British safety standards (the Lullaby Trust says if no standard number is visible you shouldn't buy it), use only the original firm, flat mattress, never add towels or duvets underneath, and keep it away from radiators, windows and blind cords.

guide.q: Can I use a travel cot as my baby's permanent bed?
guide.a: Sleep expert Mandy Gurney says travel cots are designed for short-term use because their mattresses are thinner than standard cot mattresses. They can be used safely for a while if in good condition, but for long-term sleep a full-size cot or cot bed is usually the better choice.

guide.q: How much does a travel cot cost?
guide.a: Mumsnet says prices range from about £35 to over £200 and the most expensive isn't necessarily best. Budget models like the Red Kite Sleeptight can last well into the toddler years, while pricier ones like the Bugaboo and BabyBjörn offer easier folding, better mattresses and longevity for frequent use.
